title: tune-nccl-overlap-scheduling-and-kernel-sync-for-tensor-parallel-collectives
author: Avery Chen
description:
Motivation: multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads show suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and GPU kernels for long-context generation. On our fleet, this manifests as higher p99 latency and lower sustained throughput when sequence length > 4k and TP degree >= 4. This PR improves NCCL stream scheduling, kernel/collective synchronization, and a few kernel-level changes to increase compute/comm overlap and reduce stalls.

Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a dedicated comm stream and explicit priority ordering for NCCL collectives vs compute kernels. We add a configurable stream priority map and default priorities tuned for A100/H100 hardware seen in our dedicated fleet. 2) Scheduling heuristic: the TP scheduler now inserts async barriers only when a collective would block progress and defers low-priority kernel launches so collectives can progress on the dedicated comm stream. This reduces kernel preemption of NCCL work. 3) Kernel sync changes: expose an optional non-blocking kernel-fence API that lets long-running attention kernels yield earlier to comm without incurring a full global device sync. 4) KV cache broadcast: switch KV cache broadcast to use segmented point-to-point plus NCCL for large shards to reduce tail latency on straggler GPUs. 5) Continuous batching: dispatcher heuristics were updated to be topology-aware (prefer local TPU pairs on same PCI switch for grouped batches) and to prefer batches that increase reuse of prefetched KV cache to improve amortization. 6) Tuned default NCCL collective algorithms for reduce/scatter and allgather on tensor-parallel code paths based on perf microbenchmarks.

Performance: On internal perf lab with 8xA100-40GB TP runs of 8k tokens we observe ~10-12% p99 latency reduction and 18-25% throughput uplift for sampling workloads with temperature 0.8 when using the tuned defaults vs previous master. For shorter sequences gains are smaller (~3-6%) but consistent.

Testing: added unit and integration tests that simulate TP collectives under artificial skew, including tests for KV broadcast correctness and non-blocking fence semantics. Perf tests include a new benchmark (tests/perf/tp_nccl_overlap.py) that runs in CI nightly for canary clusters.

Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag `TP_NCCL_OVERLAP_V2`. Default enabled in canary edge pool for two weeks, followed by gradual ramp to 50% of production TP traffic. Includes a rollback knob to set stream priorities back to legacy values.

Checklist:
- [x] design doc and microbenchmarks (linked in Linear ENG-4021)
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] perf benchmarks and CI coverage
- [x] ops rollout plan and rollback knobs

Notes: we intentionally avoid global device synchronizations; the non-blocking fence avoids stalls in most common attention implementations. We added extensive telemetry (per-collective latency histograms, per-stream utilization) to help detect regressions post-rollout.
commits: feat(tp): add stream priority map and dedicated comm stream
perf(tp): scheduling heuristic to prefer comm progress over low-priority kernels
fix(kernels): expose non-blocking kernel-fence and convert attention kernel path to use it
feat(kv-cache): segmented p2p + nccl broadcast path for large shards
test(perf): add tp_nccl_overlap benchmark and CI job
docs: add ops guide for NCCL tuning and rollout
review_comments: Jordan Liu: Can you clarify how the non-blocking fence differs from cudaStreamWaitEvent? Also worried about ordering semantics across multiple kernels.

Avery Chen: The fence is implemented with lightweight device-side flags and a host-side enqueue to avoid implicit global sync; it is documented in nccl_scheduler.h and we added tests that exercise reordering scenarios.
Maya Patel: We should ensure default priorities don't regress small-batch latency on low-memory instances. Suggest adding a small-batch steering config.
Avery Chen: Added small-batch steering in dispatcher and added perf tests for 1-2 token micro-batches. Results show negligible regressions and improved large-batch throughput.
Carlos Ramirez: CI gpu-integration flakes on tp_nccl_overlap on first run, reran and passed; consider adding retry transient for that job.
Avery Chen: Added retry (2 attempts) and extended timeout for the perf CI job; also added more deterministic seeding in the test harness.
release_notes: Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel performance: tuned NCCL stream scheduling, added dedicated comm stream and non-blocking kernel-fence to increase comm/compute overlap. Default tuning improves p99 latency and throughput for long-context workloads. Feature gated and rolled out gradually. See docs/ops/nccl_tuning.md for ops guidance.
